The singer was butchering Emma's song, mangled by an awkward mix of bluesy growls and sugary sweetness. Emma felt a crawling sensation on the back of her neck as she watched. She couldn't quite bring herself to get up and walk out, but her legs seemed to be stuck under the table, refusing to propel her forward.

The singer struck another wrong note, this time on purpose, and Emma winced. How could someone who claimed to have written their own music not even bother to research the original? For a moment, Lena's legs lost all feeling and she swayed, as if bracing herself against an invisible gust of wind. The beat pounded inside her chest like a jackhammer, but her feet felt rooted to the spot, refusing to budge even when someone nudged her shoulder. "Dude, you need to get in line," the stranger muttered, but Lena didn't respond.

The singer's voice swooped and dived like a wounded bird, rending her song apart from its original skeleton. A stinging sensation began to creep up Lena's nostrils, threatening to turn into full-blown panic. She needed air – or something – but still she stood there, paralyzed by an overwhelming response.

He raised a hand to brush away the wispy strand of hair escaping from under his cap, as if trying to tame some inner beast. But his eyes remained fixed on the singer's contorted face, twisted into painful grimaces above the mic stand.

When he thought things couldn't get any worse, they did. The singer added an ad-lib lyric that shredded what little music there was left, reducing his carefully crafted composition to rubble under her vocal wrecking crew. Gretchen felt a wave of dread wash over her when one kid started mucking up the verse – stumbling through the lyrics like they were reading them from a menu. The melody, the harmony... even the guitar riffs didn't sound right. Something inside Gretchen made her stumble backward against the coat rack, clinging to it like she thought the world was spinning round and around without her anymore.

The kids launched into an outro with reckless abandon, but instead of excitement or gratitude for getting her song's message across, a hollow throb inside Gretchen grew in intensity. She couldn't quite recall ever feeling this... exposed, as if the floor beneath her feet had been swept out from under her.

But something about the flyer had drawn her back – a song, "Echoes in the Night", that sounded uncannily like one of her own.

The stage manager was chatting with the opening act when Lena elbowed her way into the chaos. "What's going on here?" she asked aloud, tone still a bit hesitant from trying to navigate the crowded hallway. The lead singer, a woman with raven-black hair and an edgy grin, began singing the line Lena knew like the back of her hand – the one that started it all for her, when she'd written "Echoes" during that fateful long night.

Lena's heart started pounding in time with the music now; it felt almost physically painful. She wavered between stepping out or going back outside altogether. Something, though, seemed to hold her fastened to the spot – maybe a morbid curiosity about this strange version of her own creation. "Hey, mind if I get up close?" she said hesitantly over the music's growing din.

Something made his palms moisten without warning – which got him thinking too much about getting sweaty and awkward in front of the crowd. A part of him longed to bolt from there on an excuse or just get up and...just do what, for once? He fidgeted uncontrollably with a crumpled napkin on his lap instead.

As she started improvising over that song intro he'd worked for three years solid on perfecting, something within him gave way, like a snapped tree branch swaying before impact. It was almost loud in his ears.

"What's going on?" whispered his roommate from behind, nudging him in concern when Javier didn't respond despite leaning forward with rapt attention. Javier opened his mouth to whisper back but instead caught himself staring blankly past the singer straight at some middle-distance spot beyond her shoulder.

Her toes tapped once or twice under the alley's noiselessness before stilling into an odd little twitch. A fleeting thought shot to that particular song she had lying down to after hours last summer and what exactly might've got stuck in her head at one specific corner of a city not so far away as this... 

A hand clapped over her mouth right then, startling life back into her tapping feet – and there was something the music reminded her of again: the reason she'd written those lines in such haste and solitude. 'Why,' exactly.

"Just what do you think I wanted?" a raised voice echoed down from beyond some alley walls closer to front street; it caught her attention off guard, along with her heart pounding, somehow tied to something or rather someone up on stage right then...
